labels.notes: Row partial, unmarked (no **`label`** anywhere in the file; the title and l.12 carry the label in plain backticks). Sentence by sentence against colI_v1.tex:934-942. (1) « two singular points p̄, −p̄ corresponding to p and −p »: GX.gammaP_neg (Γ_{−p} = Γ_p), the antipodal circle GX.GammaLinkCircle.antipode (charts of L followed by linkNeg, a genuine (Γ_{−p}, ℓ(−p))-circle via hasGroupoid_comp_of_equivariant), and GX.GammaLinkCircle.DevData.isIso_flip: the flip [σ,t] ↦ [σ,π−t] is a SingularHSStructure.IsIso from 𝔢(L) onto 𝔢(L⁻) for every Δ, reading as the identity of HS² in the cone charts (cos(π−t)(−p)+sin(π−t)w = cos t p + sin t w), with south ↦ north (flip_south_north). So the link at −p̄ is L⁻. « Singular » is correctly not claimed (regular for L = ℓ(p)). (2) Time-like: positions p ∈ ℍ²₊ ⇒ −p ∈ ℍ²₋ and back; in the paper a time-like singularity's future/past quality is the position of p, so this is the sentence. (3) Light-like degree k: for every oriented lifted pair with f = δᵏ g, g with a fixed point, the antipode has an oriented lifted pair with f' = δᵏ g', g' with a fixed point, parabolic iff and hyperbolic iff kept, and every degree representation of L⁻ has the same k (degree_unique); with bdPlus ⇒ bdMinus and bdMinus ⇒ bdPlus this is the sentence and its « vice versa », with k ≥ 1 dropped (weaker hypothesis, Lean ≥ paper). (4) Cuspidal: p ∈ ∂ℍ²₊, f parabolic with a fixed point (degree 0), image = i⁺(ℓ(p)) ⇒ −p ∈ ∂ℍ²₋, parabolic degree-0 pair with image i⁺(ℓ(−p)) ∖ tangentDirs, i⁺(L⁻) = L⁻, i⁻(L⁻) = ∅. This is the paper's extreme BTZ-like past (at ∂ℍ²₋ the « similar » case of l.887-889 has I = i⁺, the directions into dS²); the removal of the two tangent directions is OQ-116 (b), disclosed; I checked the geometry by hand (B(p,w) < 0 at p gives Q(−cos s p + sin s w) > 0 at −p). (5) Space-like: the printed « always isomorphic » is replaced by the exact characterisation: moves B ∈ SO₀(1,2) with B•p = −p exist (exists_smul_eq_neg, the planner's half-turn about the time-like normal π_p(e_t)), and for every oriented lifted pair and every such B, ∃ φ, IsIsoVia C C.antipode B φ ↔ ¬(developed image ⊆ space-like directions) (isIsoVia_antipode_iff). Not vacuous: every circle has a lifted pair for every θ (GammaLinkCircle.exists_isLiftedDev, HSSingularities) and an oriented θ exists; the Misner predicate is Γ_p-invariant, so independent of the pair. Finding 1 checked and true: (a) Misner links exist at every p ∈ dS² (exists_misner: a GammaLinkCircle with an IsLiftedDev pair, hyperbolic f with a fixed point, i.e. degree 0, image in the space-like directions, exactly l.876-878's Misner case); (b) no move and no homeomorphism φ makes them IsIsoVia-isomorphic (not_isIsoVia_antipode, quantified over all B and all φ : L ≃ₜ L); (c) IsIsoVia is the natural moved-p notion and not too strict: φ reads locally as A ∘ linkMove B with A ∈ Γ_{p'}; any other B' with B'p = p' is A'B with A' ∈ Γ_{p'}, so a fixed B loses nothing; regular_isIsoVia_antipode and exists_isIsoVia_antipode (every non-Misner link, every move) show it holds where it should. The group is right: Causal.Flat.lorentz 2 is SO₀(1,2) (preserves Q, the future cone, det 1), and the paper fixes HS-surfaces as (SO₀(1,2), HS²)-structures with time-oriented de Sitter regions (l.616-623). The chirality vol3(p, π_p σ, e_t) has a constant sign on the developed Misner arc, linkNeg reverses it, and A ∘ B (det 1, orthochronous, B p = −p) keeps it; in coordinates (p = e_x, Misner arc around +e_y) every B with Bp = −p sends the +e_y arc at p to the −e_y arc at −p, while the link of −p̄ is the +e_y arc at −p. The step from links to HS-singularities (an HS-isomorphism of punctured neighbourhoods develops to some B, and here B p = −p because the developed images near p̄ lie in {⟨·,p⟩ > 0} and those near −p̄ in {⟨·,p⟩ < 0}, preserved by the hyperbolic holonomy) is argued, not formalized, and disclosed (SCOPE (b), REPORT). Note that the remark would be true under SO(1,2) (the time-reversing (t,x,y) ↦ (−t,−x,y) maps one Misner apex to the other), so the finding rests on the paper's own SO₀(1,2); OQ-120 (a) is the right place for that. Finding 2 (l.850-853 false for Misner links, argued) checked: at fixed p ∈ dS² the quotients J₊/⟨g⟩ and J₋/⟨g⟩ of the two space-like components (J₋ = J₊ + 1, δ central so g − id has one sign on both) have the same ℝP¹-circle (δ projects to the identity of ℝP¹) and empty i^±, yet no element of Γ_p maps one arc to the other (Γ_p keeps the chirality): a true finding. Finding 3 (the planner's [r] « the half-turn proves it, no ruling ») is refuted for Misner links, since not_isIsoVia_antipode holds for every B, the half-turn included. Positive/negative kept (IsSpacelikePositive.antipode etc.) and the type images kept (antipode_deSitter_image) are side results, under OQ-120 (c)/OQ-124. Readings OQ-104, OQ-113, OQ-116, OQ-120 (a)/(c), OQ-124, OQ-126 (c) are all named in the REPORT and in SCOPE (c).

findings.what: The hypothesis checklist row « future light-like of degree k ≥ 1 » is marked ✓ although the Lean theorem assumes less (k ≥ 1 not used, every k). The docstring contract (lean-causal kb/0006, which CAMPAIGN.md cites) uses ⚠ weakened for that case. The sibling files do the same (HSDegree l.57, l.59), and REPORT.json marks this hypothesis "weakened". The text of the row is true; only the symbol is wrong.
findings.fix: Write « ⚠ weakened: `p ∈ ∂ℍ²₊` and an oriented lifted holonomy `δᵏ g`, `g` with a fixed point; `k ≥ 1` not used (every `k`) ».

checks.isFutureTimelike_timeUnit: GX.isFutureTimelike_timeUnit is a two-line restatement of Causal.Flat.isFutureTimelike_timeUnit. That lemma exists only in the hub's current lean-causal (Causal/Flat/GromovBase.lean). It is absent from lean-gx's pinned lean-causal (ca2ad78, .lake/packages/Causal has no GromovBase.lean), and DEC-33 limits Causal imports in lean-gx. So the restatement is necessary, not a Reuse breach. The kb proposal should say « absent at lean-gx's lean-causal pin » rather than « which lean-gx does not import ». The names do not clash (GX vs Causal.Flat).
